Question: Which method performs the best when there are a lot of outliers in the data?
Evidence:
[E1] (text, Section 1, page 1): The cornerstone of the proposed method is a Cholesky Block in which we employ the Cholesky transform for sampling the weights of a neural network that enables us to model correlated outputs. Similar to Bayesian neural networks [ 5 ], we maintain the probability distributions over the weights, but we also leverage mixture distributions to handle the inconsistencies in a dataset. To the best of our knowledge, this is the ﬁrst approach simultaneously to infer the target distribution and the output correlations using a neural network in an end-to-end manner. We will refer to this framework as ChoiceNet . ChoiceNet is ﬁrst applied to synthetic regression tasks and a real-world regression task where we demonstrate its robustness to extreme outliers and its ability to distinguish the target distribution and noise distributions. Subsequently, we move on to image classiﬁcation tasks using a number of benchmark datasets where we show that it shows comparable or superior performances compared to existing baseline
[E2] (text, Section 4.1, page 7): The average absolute ﬁtting errors of three different functions are shown in Figure 6(a) - 6(c) , respectively where we can see that the proposed method outperforms or show comparable results with low outlier rates and shows superior performances with a high outlier rate ( > 50% ). Figure 6(d) - 6(f) show the ﬁtting results along with training data. While our proposed method is built on top of an MDN, it is worthwhile noting the severe performance degradation of an MDN with an extreme noise level ( 60% ). It is mainly because an MDN fails to allocate high mixture probability on the mixture corresponds to the target distribution as there are no dependencies among different mixtures.
[E3] (text, Section 4.1, page 7): Boston Housing Dataset A Boston housing price dataset is used to check the robustness of the proposed method. We compare our method with standard feedforward networks using four different loss functions: standard L 2 -loss, L 1 -loss which is known to be robust to outliers, a robust loss (RL) function proposed in [ 21 ], and a leaky robust loss (LeakyRL) function where the results are shown in Table 5 . Implementation details can be found in the supplementary material.

These claims are already verified and kept:
- ChoiceNet is demonstrated to be robust to extreme outliers and able to distinguish the target distribution and noise distributions.
- The proposed method outperforms or shows comparable results with low outlier rates and shows superior performances with a high outlier rate ( > 50% ).

These claims failed the checks; write corrected claims to replace them:
- "The proposed method shows comparable or superior performances compared to existing baseline.": support check: The evidence in E1 (Section 1) states that ChoiceNet shows comparable or superior performances compared to existing baselines, but it does not specify that this is the case for all outlier rates. The claim is too broad and cannot be fully supported by the evidence provided.
- "The conclusion is that ChoiceNet performs the best when there are a lot of outliers in the data.": support check: The evidence in E1 (Section 1) states that ChoiceNet demonstrates its robustness to extreme outliers and its ability to distinguish the target distribution and noise distributions, but it does not conclude that ChoiceNet performs the best when there are a lot of outliers in the data. The claim is not supported by the evidence.
